_comentario: Lines to deliver in a given voice or register. Deliberately about JOBS and SITUATIONS, never nationalities or regions: doing a news anchor is funny without being at anyone's expense.

cartas.texto: Say «I dropped my phone in the toilet» like a TV news anchor.
Say «there's no milk left» like it's the worst news of your life.
Say «nice weather today» like a nature documentary narrator.
Say «I'm getting some water» like you're in an action film.
Ask for the time like a robot running out of battery.
Say «good afternoon» like you've just run ten kilometres.
Explain how to make an omelette like a football commentator.
Say «it's my turn» in a whisper, like a state secret.
Read out the shopping list like a very sad poem.
Say «I'm hungry» like a cartoon villain.
Say thank you like you've just won a major award.
Say «the power's out» like an old-time radio announcer.
Count to five like you're falling asleep.
Say «I can't believe it» like someone who absolutely believes it.
Ask «is there any pudding left?» like you're asking after a loved one.
Say «good morning» like a ship's captain in a storm.
Explain the rules of this game like a shopping channel host.
Say «I'm going to sit down» like it's a historic decision.
Read this line like a tour guide who has lost their voice.
Say «I've lost my keys» like you're narrating the end of a novel.
Say «pass the salt» like you're talking to a newborn.
Announce that you're going to the loo like a gala host.
Say «it's so hot» like a classical stage actor.
Describe your breakfast like it's classified information.
Say «I'm off to bed» like you're leaving forever.
Ask «whose turn is it?» like a very stern judge.
Say «this tastes amazing» without using the letter E.
Introduce the person on your right like a rock star.
Say «see you later» like a shopping centre lift.
Tell everyone the time as if in a made-up language.
Say «I'm cold» like you're in space and out of oxygen.
Recite the days of the week like a magic spell.
